title: Deriving and using P = Fv practice

question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions use prior learning: q01 retrieves the definition and earlier power formula, while q07 combines work, power per unit time and P = Fv.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: prior retrieval, derivation logic, direction diagnosis, inverse use, direct multi-part use, angled-force reasoning, then a mixed derivation and consistency check

evidence_basis.originality_note: All contexts, wording, values and figure briefs are original. Official evidence grounds only the demand patterns.

questions.prompt: State the definition of power and write the formula that relates power P, work done W and time t.
Which chain of steps correctly derives P = Fv for a constant force parallel to the motion?

options.A: Use W = Ft and v = s/t, so P = F/v.
options.B: Use W = Fs and P = W/t, so P = F(s/t) = Fv.
options.C: Use P = Wt and W = Fs, so P = Fst.
options.D: Use W = Fs and v = t/s, so P = F/v.

questions.prompt: A puck moves east at constant velocity. Which force should be used as F in P = Fv when calculating the power transferred to its eastward motion?

options.A: The total magnitude of every force added without directions.
options.B: Only the force component parallel to the eastward velocity.
options.C: Only the force component perpendicular to the velocity.
options.D: The mass of the puck multiplied by its speed.

parts.label: (b)

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: The speed increases to 12 m s^-1 while the resistive force remains 180 N. Calculate the new power and state why it is greater.

questions.prompt: A tow cable pulls a survey sled across level ice. The cable tension is 2.4 kN at 25 degrees above the horizontal. The sled moves horizontally at a constant speed of 3.5 m s^-1.

figure.purpose: Assess selection and use of the tension component parallel to velocity.

figure.alt_text: A cable pulls a sled at an upward angle while the sled moves horizontally.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the component of the cable tension parallel to the velocity.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the power transferred to the sled by the cable.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why the vertical component of the cable tension makes no contribution to this mechanical power.

questions.prompt: A maintenance winch pulls a platform horizontally with a constant force of 620 N. The platform moves at a constant speed of 2.5 m s^-1 for 48 s.

parts.label: (b)

parts.label: (c)
